title: Welcome Back, America! It’s Your Turn to Be Sorry.
summary: This month, the world’s most unreliable boyfriend began to redeem himself.

Earlier this fall, when I was en route from Toronto to Boston, a security guard running the X-ray machine at Island Airport recognized me with a big smile and a warm greeting.


Then he got serious. I was in the wing of the airport reserved for U.S. travel, so he knew where I was headed. He didn’t approve.


“Minister, you know we’re not allowed to go there anymore,” he said.


I explained that I agreed with Canada’s very unofficial ban on nonessential U.S. trips. Then I assured him I was flying south to make the case for our country, and to visit an institution whose resistance to illegal orders from the White House Canadians generally admire, to boot.


He was unconvinced. “Well, Minister,” he told me, “go talk to them if that’s what you need to do. But I hope you tell those sons of bitches that we’ll be better off without them, anyway.”


I’ve told this story a few times to U.S. audiences. There is usually a collective intake of breath when I share the first line, about Canada’s de facto national boycott of discretionary U.S. visits.


That turns to astonishment, and sometimes outright anger, when I recount the kicker.


But my friend at the luggage belt was articulating the national consensus in Canada. And it is not only Canadians who have been getting ready to write off America. For many Europeans, President Trump’s recent betrayal of Ukraine has felt like the last straw, proof that America is on the wrong side in the most serious security threat the continent has faced since World War II.
